histogram.name: InitialWebUI.NewWindow{CreationSource}.{ExistingWindow}.BrowserWindow.ClosedBeforeFirstPaint{Version}
histogram.summary:
Records the duration from window creation to closing the browser window for new windows {CreationSource} {ExistingWindow} {Version}.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled, and when the initial paint has not been recorded.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.NewWindow{CreationSource}.{ExistingWindow}.BrowserWindow.FirstPaint.{StartPoint}{Version}
histogram.summary:
Records the time from {StartPoint} to 'First Paint' of the new browser window. {CreationSource} {ExistingWindow} {Version}.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.NewWindow{CreationSource}.{ExistingWindow}.BrowserWindow.ShowRequestedToFirstPaint{Version}
histogram.summary:
Records the duration from the initial show/activation request of a new browser window to its first paint. {CreationSource} {ExistingWindow} {Version}.
This metric is used to measure the impact of window show deferral. It is recorded only once per window lifecycle. If multiple windows are shown during startup, e.g. due to session restore, the first window is measured in "InitialWebUI.Startup" and not in this histogram.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.NewWindow{CreationSource}.{ExistingWindow}.BrowserWindowToReloadButton.FirstPaintGap{Version}
histogram.summary:
Records the delay between the native browser window's first presentation (paint) and the Reload Button first paint in a new window. {CreationSource} {ExistingWindow} {Version}.
This is a direct, session-linked measurement of the delta, unlike the separately logged `.FirstPaint` metrics. Used to quantify the rendering lag.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.NewWindow{CreationSource}.{ExistingWindow}.ReloadButton.{PaintType}.{StartPoint}{Version}
histogram.summary:
Records the time from {StartPoint} to first {PaintType} of the Reload Button in the new browser window. {CreationSource} {ExistingWindow} {Version}.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.ReloadButton.BrowserPaintToReloadButtonPaint{SurfaceSyncState}
histogram.summary: Records the duration from the native browser window's first presentation until the reload button first paint, with {SurfaceSyncState}. Cases where the reload button paints before browser window presentation record 0 ms.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.ReloadButton.BrowserWindowClosedBeforePaint{SurfaceSyncState}
histogram.summary: Recorded when the browser window closes after its first presentation while the reload button WebUI has not yet completed its first paint. Records the elapsed time between browser window first presentation and window closure. Sliced by {SurfaceSyncState}.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.ReloadButton.InputCount
histogram.summary:
Counts the number of times the ReloadButton is activated, sliced by input type.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.ReloadButton.InteractionToReload{InputType}
histogram.summary:
Records the latency from {InputType} user interaction with the WebUI or C++ Views reload button to the initiation of the reload command execution.
For C++ Views, the start time is the event timestamp of the click or key press, and the end time is when the browser button handler is executed. The metric is emitted immediately during the button press handler.
For WebUI, the start time is the physical interaction time reconstructed in the browser process by adding the renderer-reported interaction time offset (relative to navigation start) to the browser-side recorded navigation start ticks. The end time is when the browser process receives the Mojo reload request. The metric is emitted immediately upon validating and processing the Mojo request.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Startup.WithoutExistingWindow.ReloadButton.FirstPaint
histogram.summary: Deprecated. Removed the WithExistingWindow and WithoutExistingWindow dimension from Startup metrics, since they do not apply during startup. Records the time spent initializing a newly constructed ReloadButton in standard browser application startup. The timer starts immediately after the browser application startup, and ends immediately after a paint of the view is requested when no existing window is present.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Startup{Scenario}.BrowserWindow.ClosedBeforeFirstPaint{StartupTemperature}
histogram.summary:
Records the duration from the initial show/activation request of the first browser window during {Scenario} startup to closing the window{StartupTemperature}.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled, and when the initial paint has not been recorded.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Startup{Scenario}.BrowserWindow.FirstPaint{StartupTemperature}
histogram.summary:
Records the time from {Scenario} browser application startup to the first presentation of the browser window onto the screen{StartupTemperature}.
This metric is mutually exclusive by scenarios.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics feature is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Startup{Scenario}.BrowserWindow.ShowRequestedToFirstPaint{StartupTemperature}
histogram.summary:
Records the duration from the initial show/activation request of the first browser window during {Scenario} startup to its first paint{StartupTemperature}.
This metric is used to measure the impact of window show deferral. It is recorded only once per browser process. If multiple windows are shown during startup, e.g. due to session restore, only the first window is measured, and all the others are measured in the "InitialWebUI.NewWindow" histogram.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics feature is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Startup{Scenario}.BrowserWindowToReloadButton.FirstPaintGap{StartupTemperature}
histogram.summary:
Records the delay between the native browser window's first presentation (paint) and the Reload Button first paint during {Scenario} startup {StartupTemperature}.
This is a direct, session-linked measurement of the delta, unlike the separately logged `.FirstPaint` metrics. Used to quantify the rendering lag of the WebUI process relative to the native UI creation during heavy resource contention at startup.
This metric is mutually exclusive by scenarios.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics feature is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Startup{Scenario}.ReloadButton.RendererProcessCreated{StartupTemperature}
histogram.summary:
Records the duration from the start of {Scenario} browser application startup to the point where the dedicated renderer process for the Reload button WebUI is initialized {StartupTemperature}.
This metric specifically measures the renderer process creation cost (Cost A), which is an overhead incurred by the Initial WebUI architecture that does not exist in the native C++ Views implementation.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics feature is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Startup{Scenario}.ReloadButton.RendererProcessLaunched{StartupTemperature}
histogram.summary:
Records the duration from the start of {Scenario} browser application startup to the point where the dedicated renderer process for the Reload button WebUI is launched {StartupTemperature}.
This metrics captures the completion of the process launch sequence. Comparing this with the `.RendererProcessCreated` metric reveals the time spent in the process launch phase, specifically isolating the OS and Sandbox overhead incurred before the renderer becomes available.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics feature is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Startup{Scenario}.ReloadButton.{PaintType}{StartupTemperature}
histogram.summary:
Records the time spent initializing a newly constructed ReloadButton in the {Scenario} browser application startup with pre/post Initial WebUI setup. The timer starts immediately after the browser application startup{StartupTemperature}, and ends immediately after a {PaintType} of the view is requested.
This metric is mutually exclusive by scenarios.
For FirstPaint, the paint is requested by either the browser process (pre-Initial WebUI) or by the WebUI renderer process (post-Initial WebUI).
Only recorded on desktop platforms.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Toolbar.ParseFinishedToFirstUpdate
histogram.summary:
Records the time elapsed from when the main document finishes parsing and becomes interactive (domInteractive) to when the WebUI toolbar component completes its first rendering update (firstUpdated). This measures the latency introduced by JavaScript execution and the initial Lit component lifecycle.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics feature is enabled.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Toolbar.ProcessAlreadyExistsForTheSameProfileOnCreation
histogram.summary: Recorded during `RenderProcessHostImpl::Init()` for TopChromeWebUI processes. Records true if there is already an existing RenderProcessHost for TopChromeWebUI for the same profile that is initialized and not dead.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Toolbar.RenderProcessGone
histogram.summary:
Records the status when the Web UI Toolbar render process is terminated.
This is recorded every time when `WebUIToolbarWebView` receives `PrimaryMainFrameRenderProcessGone()` signal including the normal termination (i.e. `TERMINATION_STATUS_NORMAL_TERMINATION` and `TERMINATION_STATUS_STILL_RUNNING`).

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Toolbar.RenderProcessGoneExceedingRecoveryLimit
histogram.summary: Record the number of times that the Web UI Toolbar render process is terminated abnormmaly and it exceeds the recovery limit.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Toolbar.TimeToWindowMetricsManagerBound
histogram.summary: Recorded when the `InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager` is bound to the `InitialWebUIPageLoadMetricsObserver` after being initially unavailable (e.g., for prewarmed WebContents waiting for a BrowserWindowInterface). Measures the elapsed time from observer creation until the manager is bound.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Toolbar.TimeWithoutWindowMetricsManagerOnDestruction
histogram.summary: Recorded in `~InitialWebUIPageLoadMetricsObserver` upon destruction when no `InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager` was ever bound to the observer. Measures the elapsed time from observer creation until destruction.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.Toolbar.WindowMetricsManagerBindingStatus
histogram.summary: Recorded in `~InitialWebUIPageLoadMetricsObserver` upon destruction. Records the binding status of `InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager`: whether it was bound immediately at start, bound deferred (after receiving the `BrowserWindowInterface` change notification), or never bound before destruction.

histogram.name: InitialWebUI.View.Creation
histogram.summary:
Records the counts of key Initial WebUI views when they are created in the constructor. Use this to normalize other metrics.
This is only recorded for desktop platforms when the InitialWebUIMetrics is enabled.

This histogram is of special interest to the chrome-analysis-team@. Do not change its semantics or retire it without talking to them first.

variant.summary: Omnibox Popup

histogram.name: Views.ColorProviderCacheSize
histogram.summary: Records the size of the ColorProviderManager cache when a new ColorProvider is generated. New entries are generated when a client requests a ColorProvider with a Key that is not in the cache. Since the cache size is capped, a distribution with too many results at the tail indicate that the cache is too small.

histogram.name: Views.FocusRing.RefreshLayer.Time
histogram.summary: Records the duration of all FocusRing::RefreshLayer calls. Recorded when the focus ring's layer is refreshed. This captures fast cached cases as well as slow layer creation/destruction cases. This metric is only reported for clients with high-resolution clocks.

histogram.name: Views.FocusRing.RefreshLayer.Time.NotCached
histogram.summary: Records the duration of FocusRing::RefreshLayer calls that result in actual layer creation or destruction. Recorded when the focus ring's layer is refreshed and results in actual layer creation or destruction. This metric is only reported for clients with high-resolution clocks.

histogram.name: Views.InvalidatesDuringLayout
histogram.summary: Records the number of times a view's InvalidateLayout() method is called during a Layout() call. Calling InvalidateLayout() during a layout call should never be necessary.

histogram.name: Views.LayoutCallDepth
histogram.summary: The maximum reentrant call depth seen during a view's layout. Normally this value will be one (Layout() was not reentered). But, we know Layout() is reentered sometimes in some views (where the value will be two), and want to measure how often that is. We also want to know if Layout() is ever reentered more than two deep.

histogram.name: Views.UnnecessaryLayouts
histogram.summary: Records excess layouts of a view that will not be visible. This includes doing more than one layout between paints, or any layouts after the final paint. While some such layouts might be unavoidable in computing layout-related properties during other operations, these mostly represent unnecessary work. The zero bucket counts cases where all the layouts we did were necessary, i.e. paints that had a single preceding layout.

histogram.name: Views.{Process}.NumColorProvidersInitializedDuringOnNativeThemeUpdated
histogram.summary: Records the number of ColorProvider instances constructed and initialized by the ColorProviderManager following a NativeTheme update in a {Process} process. Emitted after the NotifyOnNativeThemeUpdated() event has been processed.

histogram.name: Views.{Process}.TimeSpentInitializingColorProvider
histogram.summary: Records the time spent initializing a newly constructed ColorProvider instance in a {Process} process. The timer starts immediately before the ColorProvider is constructed and emitted immediately after initialization (i.e. all mixers are run and the ColorMap is created).

histogram.name: Views.{Process}.TimeSpentProcessingOnNativeThemeUpdatedEvent
histogram.summary: Records the time spent synchronously processing the the NotifyOnNativeThemeUpdated() event in a {Process} process. The timer starts as soon as the event handler is entered and emitted when code returns from the event handler.

histogram.name: WebUI.ColorsStylesheetServingDuration
histogram.summary:
The time in milliseconds to generate chrome://theme/colors.css and queue it to be sent to the renderer for WebUI. Does not include url parsing time. Recorded for every request for colors.css. Lower is better.
Expired Jan 2024. Revived M124.

histogram.name: WebUI.CreatedForUrl
histogram.summary: URLs for which Chrome creates WebUIControllers.

histogram.name: WebUI.Settings.ActiveDuration
histogram.summary: The duration in milliseconds that the settings page was active (visible and focused). Recorded when the settings page is closed or navigated away. Does not include time when the page was in the background or inactive.

histogram.name: WebUI.Settings.PathVisited
histogram.summary:
Paths within chrome://settings visited. For evaluating popularity and priorities for chrome://settings GUI. Note that this metric used to include paths that were part of OS settings, but starting with M-81, this metric only records browser settings paths.
For Android settings usage check Settings.FragmentAttached.

histogram.name: WebUI.ShownUrl
histogram.summary: WebUI URLs that are shown to the user. For WebUIs that don't have a WebUI object (e.g. chrome://dino), recorded on the network request. For others, recorded on commit if not preloaded. For preloaded WebUIs, recorded when WebUIContentsPreloadManager::Request() is invoked. This differs from WebUI.CreatedForUrl as it only logs WebUIs that are actually shown (i.e., a preloaded WebUI may never be shown).

histogram.name: WebUI.TopChrome.Preload.Reason
histogram.summary: The reason of preloading a WebUI. Logged when a preloaded WebUI is created.

histogram.name: WebUI.TopChrome.Preload.Result
histogram.summary: The result of attempting to use a preloaded WebUI when a new Top Chrome WebUI is requested.

histogram.name: WebUI.TopChrome.RequestToFCP{WebUIName}
histogram.summary: Measures the time elapsed from the initiation of a WebUI request to its first contentful paint. This metric applies to the main frame documents of top-chrome WebUI pages, such as side-panel content. The request initiation is marked by the call to WebUIContentsPreloadManager::Request().

histogram.name: WebUI.TopChrome.RequestToLCP{WebUIName}
histogram.summary: Measures the time elapsed from the initiation of a WebUI request to its largest contentful paint. This metric applies to the main frame documents of top-chrome WebUI pages, such as side-panel content. The request initiation is marked by the call to WebUIContentsPreloadManager::Request().

histogram.name: WebUI.WebUIURLLoaderFactory.URLRequestLoadTime
histogram.summary: The elapsed time for URL requests made through the WebUIURLLoaderFactory. The reported duration is the time spent in the browser process from the reception of the mojo request up to the content delivery through mojo call.

histogram.name: WebUICodeCache.FeatureEnabled
histogram.summary: True if WebUICodeCache feature is enabled. This counts the number of times generated WebUICodeCache JS code cache is instantiated.

histogram.name: WrenchMenu.MenuAction
histogram.summary: Number of times that each menu item is clicked.

histogram.name: WrenchMenu.TimeToAction{Action}
histogram.summary: The time a user takes to select a menu item after opening the menu.
